messages.author: 1e1f02e079119aa4
messages.subject: Predictions involving group effects
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to generate model-averaged predictions following a pcount
analysis using study area ("site") as a group effect. When I don't
include any "site" models in the model set fms, it works fine. But
when I include "site" models, I get the following error message:

Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = "contr.treatment") :
contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels

My code is below. What I'm trying to do is get model-averaged
estimated abundance across the range of the variable "clouded", while
holding the other variables constant. "logged" is another sitecov.
"trail", "studyday", and "camhours" are obscovs. For the predictions,
I chose a site ("Ulu_Padas") that I thought had approximately average
conditions.

newData<-data.frame(clouded=seq(-1.4,3.6,,50),
logged=median(logged.z), trail=median(trail.z), studyday=1,
camhours=1, site="Ulu_Padas")

E.N.bar<-predict(fms, type="state", newdata=newData, appendData=TRUE)

Any suggestions for how to make this work?

Thanks so much in advance.

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Predictions involving group effects
parts:
Hi Jaya,

The solution can be found here: https://groups.google.com/d/topic/unmarked/5UnUR4Ui4wA/discussion

You just need to specify site as a factor with all the levels (vector of unique site names) defined as follows:

newData<-data.frame(..., site=factor("Ulu_Padas",levels=site.names))
